RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 3

An all-male panel selected a male candidate over you, another man. The panel's composition can't plausibly have disadvantaged you on grounds of sex — there's no asymmetry to exploit. Raising it would look like grasping, and risks undermining the complaint you do have.

Your real grievance is procedural: you asked for written reasons two weeks ago and got nothing. In most jurisdictions you're entitled to a reasoned explanation, often within a set deadline. Send a follow-up in writing, cite the original date, and ask specifically how the criteria were scored — particularly how "experience of leading international projects" was weighted against your law degree, policy master's and ten years' service. If silence continues, escalate to HR or the ministry's appeals route.
